    UPDATE 2026-04-27: real cause found, fixed in v1.1.1. Sticky is rewritten because the previous version got the diagnosis wrong.

    Massive thanks to Hawk243, who DMed me his R5.log and the first lines made the bug obvious. Four days of wrong theories collapsed in about 30 seconds:

    R5LogCheck: Class of type '' doesnt exists. Asset: /Game/Paks/~mods/ShareShip/mod
    R5LogJsonAssets: Cannot create asset: '/Game/Paks/~mods/ShareShip/mod'


    DamianKrat had also called this exact fix in the thread below back on April 23, and the old sticky waved him off. Wrong call, sorry Damian.

    What was actually broken: the v1.0.0 and v1.1.0 release zips contained three UE4SS leftover files (mod.json, enabled.txt, Scripts/main.lua) that I left in from an early dev iteration. The IoStore pak loader ignores them, which is why I assumed they were inert. They are not. Windrose's own R5JsonAssets plugin auto-scans every *.json under ~mods/ and tries to build a UObject out of each one. The UE4SS-style mod.json has no Class field, R5JsonAssets throws, and the splash damage matches every report in this thread: journal and discoveries UI gone, backpack mods losing their slot bumps, fast-travel hangs on dedicated.

    Fix: install v1.1.1 (Nexus + GitHub), or just open <install>\R5\Content\Paks\~mods\ShareShip\ and delete mod.json, enabled.txt, and the Scripts/ folder. Same result either way. The .pak / .ucas / .utoc bytes are unchanged from v1.1.0, the feature itself didn't move.

    First published mod, shipped a folder of dev leftovers right next to the three files that actually do the work. The pak loader didn't care, the JSON plugin cared a lot. Lesson absorbed. Sorry for the broken saves, please update.

    If you're STILL seeing trouble after v1.1.1:
    - Don't use Vortex for Windrose mods, manual install only.
    - BackPacks10x and ShipInventory10x had their own packing-tool issues around April 21 to 23 (unrelated to ShareShip). Grab TheHeechee's post-April-23 re-uploads if you use either.
    - Otherwise post your R5.log (%LocalAppData%\R5\Saved\Logs\R5.log) and the ~mods folder contents and I'll keep digging.

    Thanks for the patience, and especially thanks to Hawk243 for the log that nailed it.

    Appreciate the list, StellaSoleil - and no worries, everyone has that blind spot about their own modlist.

    Looking at it, I think you and I are landing on the same suspect: More Fast Travel and Bonfires. And yeah - it being a legacy .pak-only mod sitting alongside ShareShip's IoStore container is almost certainly where the conflict lives. Let me write out what I've figured out about how Windrose loads these, because it's messier than it looks on the surface.

    Windrose (UE 5.6.1) ships with the IoStore packaging format - that's why the "normal" mods in your list are 3-file triples (.pak + .utoc + .ucas). IoStore routes every asset read through FIoDispatcher using a global chunk-ID system, and priority is basically "last container to mount wins for any chunk ID it claims." Legacy .pak-only mods take the other path through the old FPakPlatformFile pipeline. In a mixed environment (Windrose supports both), whichever system has the more recent registration for a given cooked asset wins - and that ordering is fragile, not strictly deterministic across game patches.

    Where ShareShip is very likely part of the problem: in v1.0 / v1.1 I built the IoStore container with a mount scope that's wider than what I'm actually patching. I only edit two DataAssets (the helm interaction option + the steering wheel interaction target), but the container's TOC registers a bigger chunk range than that. If More Fast Travel and Bonfires is patching fast-travel-related assets that also fall inside that range, my container may be shadowing its override with… effectively nothing, because I don't actually ship content for those slots. That would explain why fast travel still triggers but the replacement logic never resolves cleanly - the server just sits there waiting for data that was supposed to come from the other mod. That's on me, not on them. Narrowing the scope in v1.2 is what should fix it.

    Honest side note, since you've clearly been deep in server modding: I came into UE modding from Factorio (Lua, very isolated data.raw overrides), Valheim (Harmony C# patching, non-destructive runtime hooks), and Hytale (JS plugin API, also runtime-level). All three of those ecosystems let two mods usually coexist because they patch at runtime, not by binary-replacing cooked assets. UE5 pak modding is a completely different mindset - you ship pre-cooked binaries that rewrite specific FObjectImport byte ranges, and everything is "last writer wins" at the container level. No sandbox, no mod loader resolving conflicts, the community just has to work around it. I'm still climbing that learning curve and I won't pretend I've fully understood the mount-priority dance yet. v1.2 should be a big step, but if you've hit clean patterns in your tech work that play nicely alongside legacy .pak mods, I'd genuinely love to hear what's worked.

    Thanks again for digging into this with me.

      That makes a lot of sense. That would probably be the hook that's catching. 
      It's waiting for something, but since it doesn't get it-- it just... locks up for a second. 
      Very literally 'cannot compute' haha. Sadly while tech is amazing, it takes things a bit too literal sometimes.

      Ahh, yes, I have worked with Valheim, Hytale, Palworld, Minecraft, Subnautica, Rune Factory... I've been around a few. 
      So, while I haven't poked UE5 specific tools (Are there any now? Maybe I'm getting old over here LOL), UE4SS does work on UE5. And it is much more elegant and compatible as you've stated. .pak mods have always been the most 'early but effective' modding method there is for most of these games. They are brutally effective at what they do, but because of how they work? They're extremely prone to breakage from updates, conflicts, etc. 

      Right now, for Windrose, UE4SS is in infancy, due to the game being so young. But it does exist, even has been custom tailored by a member of the community for compatibility. And in fact is supported even on dedicated. Most hosts (including the one I work for even, I won't namedrop, not here to advert) are running Windrose on WINE and Proton so all you need to really do is simply add a line to target the .dll in order to locate and load it even on Linux systems. I'm working with my Manager right now to add support for it in our systems as we speak. 

      I feel you with the .pak vs script mods. It's a huge difference in the ease of use and how you can put these files together certainly. A lot more limiting. But I've seen most games start out this way then progress into another system or subsystem if the game blows up. Windrose is a week in and already has a few UE4SS mods, so we're off to a good start. Honestly, I hope the community adopts UE4SS sooner rather than later as they're far less prone to breakage during updates in comparison to .pak mods. Trying to sort load order too is a thing. You can never assure someone will be putting it the right way with .pak mods. It's a bit rough and chaotic. But... they're effective. Very effective. Just... rough. LOL.

      Honestly, most times people just sort of do the best they can with .pak until a secondary system comes along, or curate a list that doesn't explode with each other somehow. It's a balancing act. 

      Also the fact you started with Factorio is fun! Actually something we host but ironically I've never gotten to work on as it's not that popular.
